title: NL coast: easy hour, firm sand
terrain: firm wet sand at the waterline, flat, no dunes today
coachNotes: FUELLING TARGET RAISED 60 -> 80 g/h ON 24 AUG. THIS SUPERSEDES EVERY 60 g/h TARGET BELOW. Products checked: Enervit Carbo Gel C2:1 Pro is 40g of carbohydrate per 60ml gel at a 2:1 glucose-fructose ratio, roughly double a normal gel, and the fructose clears the single-transporter ceiling that set the old 60 target. SiS GO Isotonic is 22g and maltodextrin only, i.e. glucose pathway only, 10mg sodium. GUT TRAINING ON ANY RUN OVER AN HOUR: 2 Enervit gels per hour, one on the hour and one on the half hour. WATER IS NOT OPTIONAL WITH THESE GELS: 40g in 60ml is about a 66% solution, strongly hypertonic, and taken dry it pulls water into the gut. 150-250ml of water with every gel. Do not stack a SiS gel on top of 2 Enervit, it is glucose only and pushes you past the ~60 g/h glucose ceiling without adding fructose. Transporter capacity adapts over roughly two weeks of repeated exposure, so this starts now or it does not happen before 5 September. Last day of the flat block, fly home tonight. Easy hour, nothing to prove. NO DUNES TODAY: Saturday took the vertical and the calves will know it, and a second sand-climbing day 48h apart two weeks out is how a new surface turns into an Achilles problem. Flat firm sand only. BEACH CAMBER: turn around every 10-15 minutes so the same leg is not on the low side for an hour, or run the flattest band above the high tide line. A canted surface is a documented ITBS provoker and it is the one avoidable risk on this beach. If the calves are sore from Saturday, run the road instead and lose nothing. GUT TRAINING: 60 g/h from minute 30, on this run too, easy or not. Transporter capacity adapts over roughly two weeks of repeated exposure, so every run over an hour between now and 5 September is part of the adaptation. Carbohydrate in the bottle rather than chewing your way there. Next weekend is the Alps and 5 September is the last specific day, so land Monday intact rather than fit.
